title: Transcontinental routing cartography: latency tiers, soft-pin affinity, and graceful capacity pruning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a durable, explainable multi-region routing layer that treats regions like map tiles in a routing 'cartography'. This ticket implements a latency-tiered dispatcher with soft-pin affinity and a capacity-pruning (graceful load shedding) controller that cooperates with circuit breakers. The goal is to keep tail-latency SLOs for interactive hosted API customers while minimizing cross-region egress and unnecessary model fallbacks during short capacity spikes.

Problem statement:
- Current steering logic treats region preference as a hard binary or as a single-weight heuristic. Under bursts, this causes noisy mass-evacuations or expensive hedges that increase egress and cost.
- We lack a consistent way to express per-customer locality preference vs. SLO tradeoffs and to gradually degrade locality when capacity is constrained.

Objectives:
1) Implement latency-tier dispatch: each candidate region is scored by measured p50/p95/p99 latency bands and a weighted cost penalty. Regions are classified into tiers (Preferred, Nearby, Remote).
2) Soft-pin affinity: keep placement affinity for customer tokens with a hysteresis window; allow probabilistic pin-stepping instead of immediate re-pin on failures.
3) Capacity pruning controller: when regional headroom dips below configured thresholds, progressively prune routing fanout and reduce allowed concurrency per token using grace levels (green/yellow/red) rather than immediate hard rejects.
4) Circuit breaker handshake: integrate with regional circuit breakers so pruning decisions are informed by circuit state (tripped, cooling, healthy).

Design notes (high level):
- Scoring: region_score = alpha * normalized_latency + beta * cost_multiplier + gamma * (1 - headroom_fraction). Latency is a composite of p95 and p99 windows (default: 70% p95, 30% p99). Tunables stored in config service.
- Tiering: scores bucketed into three tiers with configurable boundaries. Tier transitions use exponential backoff to avoid oscillation.
- Soft-pin: a token maintains a preferred_region, last_success_ts, and a stability_counter. On marginal failures, stability_counter decremented; only after counter <= 0 and hysteresis timeout expires will we probabilistically step to a nearby tier region (probability increases linearly with consecutive failures).
- Pruning levels: 
  * Green (>25% headroom): full fanout allowed.
  * Yellow (10-25%): disable hedging to remote regions; reduce max in-flight per token by 30%.
  * Red (<10%): restrict to Preferred only if healthy; otherwise return user-facing 429 with explanatory error code.
- Circuit breakers: expose simple callback interface: regionState(region_id) -> {state: healthy|cooling|tripped, cooling_until: ts}. Pruning logic treats cooling as partial capacity loss (apply gamma penalty).

API / Config changes:
- Add /routing/policies/{policy_id} object with fields: latency_weights, cost_weight, headroom_thresholds, pin_hysteresis_ms, stability_counter_init, tier_boundaries. Policy visible in Console under Routing -> Policies.
- SDK: readonly endpoint to query effective routing decision for a sample token (for debugging only).

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for scoring, tier transitions, soft-pin state machine, and pruning thresholds.
- End-to-end simulation harness demonstrates that under a synthetic regional spike (50% capacity loss for 90s) the system moves from Green->Yellow->Red and reverts cleanly without mass cross-region flooding.
- 1% or less increase in cross-region egress in steady-state compared to current baseline; tail P99 under degraded region meets SLOs for 95% of simulated customers.
- Feature flag gated rollout with metrics dashboards: routing_decision.rate, region_headroom.gauge, pruning_level.count, soft_pin.reassignments.count, cross_region_egress.bytes.

Telemetry and metrics:
- Emit decision_reason with each routed request (tier, score components, circuit_state). Decision_reason is a short code (e.g., T2_CAP_PRUNE_CB).
- Track per-token affinity age distribution.
- Alert when soft_pin.reassignments.rate > 0.5%/min or when pruning_level.Red persists > 2m for major regions.

Testing plan:
- Local unit tests + property tests for score monotonicity.
- Simulation: reuse load-sim harness from ENG-456291 to run multi-region sequences and assert rollback behavior.
- Canary: enable for 1% of traffic in us-east-1 default policy; monitor charts for 24h; run canary burn-in with controlled simulated regional capacity reductions.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: oscillation across regions under flapping network conditions. Mitigation: use backoff, add minimal dampening TTL, require multiple p95 breaches before stepping tiers.
- Risk: misconfigured thresholds can hurt locality. Mitigation: default conservative thresholds; Console warns on low headroom thresholds; gradual ramp via feature flag.

Follow-ups:
- Expose per-customer SLA sensitivity knob in Console to bias score toward locality or strict latency.
- Explore machine-learned tier boundaries in runtime-1.25 if static thresholds insufficient.
updates: 2026-03-03: Initial scoping session with PM (Lena Cho) and SRE (Daniel Kim). Agreed on three-tier model and soft-pin state machine.

2026-03-05: Design review w/ infra and console teams. Console needs routing policy UI hooks. Created Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Transcontinental+Routing+Cartography.
2026-03-07: Spike implementation: scoring function and tierer prototype in repo infra/steering/cartographer. Demoed to team; prototype passes synthetic latency shaping tests.
2026-03-10: PR opened for base scoring & soft-pin state machine: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4127 (WIP). Writing unit tests and simulation harness integration.
2026-03-12: SRE asked to add additional telemetry fields (decision_reason and token_affinity_age). Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12: Blockers: need circuit-breaker API stub from ENG-100312; pinged owner for pruning callback spec.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy object can be created and viewed in Console and has sane defaults.
Scoring and tiering have unit coverage with edge cases (NaN, missing headroom) handled.
Simulation shows stable graceful degradation without large cross-region egress spikes under 3 synthetic regional fault scenarios.
Canary rollout completes with no regressions to production P99 latency and per-route cost increases within target (<=2%).
rollout_steps: Unit tests + simulation harness run on CI.
Deploy scoring/tiering logic to runtime staging.
Enable for 1% traffic in us-east-1; monitor 24h.
Gradually increase to 10% then 50% with metric gates.
monitoring_plan: Dashboards: routing_decisions (by tier), region_headroom, cross_region_egress, soft_pin.reassignments.
SLO alerts: P95/P99 per-route and global; pruning_level.Red > 2m per-region alert.
Runbook: if global cross_region_egress > baseline + 10% for >10m, revert feature flag immediately and engage on-call steering lead.
